bull_case: Multi-generation custom-XPU design wins, Ethernet networking and increasingly non-terminable VCF contracts reinforce switching costs across silicon, fabric and software. Scale allows Broadcom to fund R&D across several infrastructure layers.
bear_case: Custom silicon architectures are ultimately customer-controlled; hyperscalers can internalize design or multi-source. Broadcom has limited classic network effects or user-data flywheels, so its moat depends more on engineering execution and switching costs than ecosystem lock-in.
thesis: The moat is widening through design-in switching costs and software contract durability, but it is not a closed platform moat. Pricing/switching and multi-layer technical capability are strong; measurable network/data ecosystem feedback remains limited, which keeps the domain below Compounder threshold.

evidence.claim: The majority of new software contracts no longer had termination-for-convenience provisions by Q3 FY2026, while VCF demand drove infrastructure software growth.
OpenAI and Meta announced multi-generation custom-AI accelerator programs with Broadcom, including networking components and gigawatt-scale deployments.
evidence.source: Broadcom official OpenAI 2026-06-24 and Meta 2026-04-14 announcements

evidence.claim: Q3 gross margin increased to 69% from 67% y/y despite a higher semiconductor mix, which management notes carries lower gross margin than infrastructure software.
RPO was approximately $179.2B and included long-term custom-AI obligations; approximately 25% was expected to convert over the next 12 months.
The AI XPV platform targets more than 20GW of compute through 2028 and coordinates Broadcom XPUs/networking with external financial partners and customer leases.
Top-five end customers represented about 55% of Q3 revenue and one distributor represented 50%, increasing the bargaining power of a small customer/channel set.

counterevidence: The custom-XPU buyer owns workload data and architecture decisions, so it can shift suppliers over generations.
RPO and GW capacity measure commercial scale, not a self-reinforcing developer/user network.
High customer concentration can transfer part of the economic moat to customers through bargaining power.
No disclosed market-share time series proves that Broadcom's share is structurally rising across all AI infrastructure layers.
unknowns: Customer switching cost measured in dollars/time between custom-XPU suppliers.
Broadcom's custom-AI accelerator market share and change over time.
Long-run pricing for successive XPU generations.
falsifiers: Moat trajectory weakens if a major customer shifts two generations away from Broadcom without replacement wins.
Switching/pricing score falls if gross margin compresses below 60% without an offsetting software mix change.
Ecosystem score rises only if Broadcom discloses repeatable scale/trend metrics rather than contract value alone.

hard_veto_flags.rationale: The veto requires actual and persistent shrinkage. Current evidence shows expanding AI revenue, improving consolidated gross margin, multi-generation design wins and tighter software contracts. Future customer insourcing is a monitoring risk, not evidence that the moat is already persistently shrinking.

next_checks: Obtain customer-switching case studies and XPU supplier transition costs.
Track custom-XPU and Ethernet market share separately.
Look for repeatable ecosystem participant metrics rather than contract value.

subscores.rationale: Multi-generation custom-silicon design-ins, tighter VCF contracts and a 69% consolidated gross margin support the 75 strengthening anchor. 90 is excluded because customer concentration and architecture ownership constrain pricing power.

RPO and XPV capacity provide 1-2 usable scale proxies, but no same-definition user/developer/partner trend or quantified switching case is disclosed. The observable table therefore maps to 55 rather than 75.

Custom silicon engineering, Ethernet networking and infrastructure software are distinct defense layers, fitting the 75 multiple-defense anchor. 90 is excluded because hyperscalers can internalize silicon design and standards remain open enough to multi-source.

uncertainties.rationale: Design-in costs are evident qualitatively but not quantified.
Commercial scale is not the same as a network-effect flywheel.
The strongest potential substitute is the customer itself.
